sections.name: Police: LSPD, sheriff and Highway Patrol
sections.card:
Summary: The Los Santos Police Department (LSPD) covers the city of Los Santos, its airport and its port, the Los Santos County Sheriff's Department (LSSD) covers Blaine County as well, and the San Andreas Highway Patrol (SAHP) patrols the highways on Police Bikes.
Weak points: A gunshot to the legs kills an LSPD officer or sheriff's deputy, either at once or by blood loss. Officers are known to take cover behind or stand near a burning car that is about to explode.
Tips: The sheriff's deputies drive and fight just like the LSPD, in Sheriff Cruisers.
Tips: Highway Patrol officers shoot Pistols at you once you fire a weapon or reach two stars; those who spawned on a bike chase you on it, and those who spawned standing only chase on foot, though they may take civilian cars.

sections.name: Police at one and two stars
sections.card:
Summary: At one star officers, soldiers and security guards chase you, and police and soldiers try to arrest you at gunpoint. At two stars police shoot to kill, drive much more aggressively to ram you off the road, and at least three police cars chase you.
Weak points: At one star the police only hold you at gunpoint, and fighting back or running away raises it to two stars at once. Security guards and police on motorcycles open fire straight away instead of arresting you.
Tips: At two stars police cars may wait at the roadside to ambush you, or blend into traffic with their lights and sirens off until you draw near.
Tips: Police only try a vehicular arrest after a chase has lasted about a minute without you hurting any cop and you stop your vehicle.

sections.name: Police at three stars
sections.card:
Summary: At three stars police set up roadblocks of police cars and police transporters, sometimes with a spike strip laid out behind them, and a Police Maverick helicopter shadows you with NOOSE TRU officers riding on board.
Weak points: The helicopter stays on station until every rifleman on board is killed, then returns to base, but another one replaces it in short order. At night it shines a spotlight on you so the ground units can find you.
Tips: Every officer who spawns at three stars or more wears a bulletproof vest, and officers run up to a car you have stopped in, drag you out and kill you on the spot, so keep moving.

sections.name: NOOSE TRU at four and five stars
sections.card:
Summary: At four stars NOOSE TRU teams come to kill you, three officers to a vehicle, in FIB Grangers in Los Santos or Sheriff SUVs in Blaine County, with two hanging off the sides firing at you while more shoot from Police Mavericks overhead. At five stars the streets fill with police and almost no civilian traffic.
Weak points: They wear body armour and do not lose health quickly, but a single headshot kills them even in a helmet, and any gunshot to the legs kills them at once or by blood loss.
Tips: If you hole up in a building or behind tight cover they use tear gas to force you out, and a Police Maverick may land or rappel four officers down to you.
Tips: Shooting down a pursuing Police Maverick can itself raise you to four stars, though it may take two or more downed units.

sections.name: Soldiers and Rhino tanks at Fort Zancudo
sections.card:
Summary: The military is never called in to chase you, but near Fort Zancudo soldiers in Crusaders and Barracks join a chase and try to arrest you, and on the base itself they shoot to kill.
Weak points: A Rhino tank takes about 3 to 4 tank shells, 5 to 6 RPG shots or 7 to 8 Grenade Launcher shots to blow up, and a hit on its rear may open the fuel tank, so that a lit fuel trail stops it after a few minutes, though its turret keeps working.
Tips: Soldiers fire a Rocket Launcher at an aircraft if it is hijacked in the base or you are flying one of them, and patrolling Rhinos may leave the base to chase you, using their cannons, if you stay too close for too long.
Tips: Entering the base gives four stars; flying over it gives two, which quickly become four if you do not move away; and firing any rocket from an aircraft gives five stars at once.

sections.name: Ballas
sections.card:
Summary: A large African American street gang in purple who control almost all of Davis, with the cul-de-sac of Grove Street a hot spot, and a traditional rivalry with the Families.
Weak points: Most of them stand on the sidewalks in groups of 3 to 5 and carry pistols and knives.
Tips: They usually leave you alone if you walk through their territory, but they turn hostile if you taunt them enough, fire a gun there or just stand near and stare, and then they shoot, stab or punch you; their dogs sometimes attack too.
Tips: Starting a gunfight with a gang, or killing several of its members in a row, gives you two stars.

sections.name: The Lost MC
sections.card:
Summary: A motorcycle club whose Los Santos chapter patrols the East Vinewood area in Gang Burritos and runs a clubhouse there, with a hideout in Stab City.
Weak points: Some ride in small groups of two or three, on Hexer, Daemon and Sovereign bikes.
Tips: After the main story you can still meet them at their East Vinewood clubhouse, Hookies in North Chumash, R L Hunter & Sons in Grapeseed and Stab City.
Tips: If they run into Trevor, they attack him on sight.

sections.name: Sharks
sections.card:
Summary: Sharks in GTA V are fast, dangerous predators that often attack on sight. They spawn more often at night, show on the minimap as a red dot, stalk and circle you for a while before attacking, and sometimes come in pairs.
Weak points: From a boat one shot kills a shark, so look out for them and kill them from the surface before you dive. You can also run into one with a boat or Submersible, or stab it with a knife over and over, which is extremely difficult.
Tips: A shark kills with its first bite even if you have full health and armor. If you are too deep or too far out to get back to your boat or the shore, swim into sunken plane and ship ruins, which often makes the shark swim away.
Tips: The Hammerhead Sharks added on PC, PlayStation 4 and Xbox One never attack, and if you reach the end of the map a shark is scripted to appear and kill you.

sections.name: Cougars
sections.card:
Summary: Large wild cats found in forested and hilly areas from the Vinewood Hills to Mount Chiliad. A cougar growls loudly when it is near, then relentlessly charges, pounces and kills you instantly with a throat bite.
Weak points: A cougar runs away if you are driving or firing a weapon and will not attack if you are on top of a vehicle. If you react quickly you can kill or knock out one by kicking it.
Tips: Trevor's special ability lets him survive a cougar attack with no damage.
Tips: In the Hunting side activity cougars spawn often and show as a red circle on the map, like deer, which often tricks you into walking right into an attack.

sections.name: Body Armor
sections.card:
Summary: A protective blue vest in five tiers, all bought from Ammu-Nation: Super Light (20%) for $500, Light (40%) for $1,000, Standard (60%) for $1,500, Heavy (80%) for $2,000 and Super Heavy (100%) for $2,500.
Uses: Armor pads your health against gunfire, explosions and fire, and in GTA V it also protects you from falls and impacts again. Each tier adds another 20%.
Tips: Climbing into a Police Riot gives you armor. It shows as a blue bar next to your health bar below the radar.

sections.name: Health, snacks and vending machines
sections.card:
Summary: Your health refills by itself only back to the halfway point: when it falls below 50% it recovers up to 50% if you stand still and do not walk or run.
Uses: Snacks from convenience stores heal you and are eaten as you buy them: P’s & Q’s cost $1, EgoChaser $2 and Meteorite Bar $4, and each heals a different amount. Sprunk or eCola from a vending machine costs $1.
Tips: Snacks can also be shoplifted or dropped by dead enemies and pedestrians, and vending machines are not marked on the map.
Tips: In GTA V you cannot buy food from street vendors or restaurants; the only food you can buy is snacks from convenience stores.

sections.name: Parachute
sections.card:
Summary: A $100 parachute from Ammu-Nation, unlocked after the mission Minor Turbulence; getting into any aircraft also gives you one.
Uses: After the parachute opens you can fire handguns and single-handed submachine guns. You can open it from a falling bike, but the bike cannot be carried and falls without you.
Tips: Pull back on the movement stick to land safely: pushing forward makes you faceplant, which may injure or kill you.
Tips: The chute is vulnerable to gunfire and to nearby explosions that set it on fire, and a ripped chute detaches and sends you falling.

sections.name: Rhino Tank
sections.card:
Summary: A 60-ton battle tank with a 120mm cannon. You can buy it for $3,000,000 from Warstock Cache & Carry, and it then spawns in your aircraft hangar, or you can hijack one at Fort Zancudo.
Uses: The cannon fires every 1.5 seconds, reaches 190 meters and is very effective against most targets, and the tracks crush small vehicles, which either explode or catch fire. You cannot be busted easily inside it.
Tips: Keep the cannon off close targets in tight spaces such as alleyways, because the shell can explode right beside the tank and damage it.
Tips: The gun is a solid part of the tank, so light poles, traffic lights and walls can block your aim or even get you stuck.

sections.name: Stun Gun
sections.card:
Summary: A handgun by Coil that fires a probe to stun a target and takes about 4 seconds to recharge. You get it in the mission Monkey Business and can buy it afterwards at Ammu-Nation for $100.
Uses: A stunned person drops and cannot get up, and usually does not survive, although street criminals and animals sometimes get up as if nothing happened. A shot to the head drops them at once, and a person in a vehicle may fall out of it.
Tips: Its range is only slightly longer than most melee weapons. It counts as a handgun, so it works for drive-bys, but with low damage and a low fire rate; it can also shoot out the tires of vehicles that are not bulletproof, and kill people.

sections.name: Sticky Bombs
sections.card:
Summary: A throwable plastic explosive with a remote detonator: you throw it and then detonate it, or attach it to a vehicle and then detonate it. It costs $400 and is unlocked by the mission Friends Reunited.
Uses: They stick to any vehicle and can be set off at any time, somewhat like landmines, but in story mode they cannot stick to pedestrians. A Rhino in free roam can be destroyed with three of them.
Tips: Keep your own car out of the blast radius, because shooting a placed bomb sets it off, and so does ramming one stuck to a vertical surface.
Tips: You can have 20 placed at once, the 21st removes the first, and they never explode on their own.
